item.title: Operation Master: Deconstructing a Multi-Tiered Intrusion and Monetization Pipeline
item.description:
Operation Master exposed: a single Brazilian 🇧🇷 threat actor ran a full intrusion-to-fraud pipeline, exploiting CVE-2026-0257 across 7 GlobalProtect gateways in four countries, stealing 600+ companies' data, then weaponizing it inside an automated multi-tenant invoice fraud platform that generated 2.4M+ messages and R$150.4M in attempted PIX fraud.
- CVE-2026-0257 (GlobalProtect authentication bypass) was the primary at-scale access vector. The actor forged auth cookies from target certificate context and fed candidates through a 30-worker automated exploit loop driven by continuous masscan output across 277.5M scanned hosts. The same CVE is being exploited separately by ransomware actors including Qilin, making it a high-priority patch target. Beyond VPN access, parallel campaigns hit SQLi targets via sqlmap and xp_cmdshell chains to pivot from database access to host execution, with DNS subdomain tunneling (470,268 queries from a single compromised host, structured as task.row.chunk.base64.x.random.victim-hostname) as the primary exfil rail, and rclone syncing to MEGA as a redundant second channel. Staged webshells (beacon.dll, wmsvc.dll, gopher_new.exe) and AdaptixC2 on 91.92.241[.]187 (ports 8443/4444/4321) provided C2 over HTTP and raw TCP. Additional techniques: SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hive theft (T1003.002), ntds.dit recovery (T1003.003), GodPotato token impersonation, PwnKit (CVE-2021-4034), CVE-2024-1086, and CVE-2023-7028 (CVSS 10.0 GitLab dual-email reset) hardcoding cyberkill2025[@]gmail.com as the attacker-controlled recovery address.
- The fraud monetization layer is a Node.js multi-tenant "master-panel" at /opt/master-panel/, running under PM2, backed by PostgreSQL and SQLite, and exposed externally on yzs[.]fi. Lookalike domains igreenfaturas[.]to, wattiofaturas[.]com, and nuvfaturas[.]com hosted per-victim invoice pages with URL parameters embedding the victim's real name, due date, consumption, and billing amount pulled from stolen utility databases. Email delivery routed through 12 hijacked M365 mailboxes (retail, healthcare, education) to inherit sender reputation. SMS ran across 8 SMPP gateways. PIX payments routed through a serverless Vercel proxy at pix-proxy-sable.vercel[.]app. The lead source was 1.8M records scraped via a passwordless JWT flaw in iGreen Energia's API. The fraud engine logged 622,666 personalized links, 317,696 click events, and R$38.9M in fraudulent invoices opened by victims.
- Attribution converges on forum persona masterblack and primary email cyberkill2025[@]gmail.com, which appears across: 34 fraud panel lead test records, the GitLab CVE-2023-7028 exploit hardcoding, OSINT API registrations (Shodan, VirusTotal, SecurityTrails, WPScan, AlienVault OTX), a recovered pentest report listing the operator, and a leaked hacker forum database record directly linking the email to the masterblack account that sold stolen iGreen and Wattio data weeks before the fraud campaigns began. The two-stage strategy, sell the data first, then phish the same victims with their own billing records, is confirmed by the 9 to 14 week gap between forum sale listings and bulk tenant seeding. The operator's AI agent workspace (36+ offensive subagents, ~45 persistent memory files) was exposed via a misconfigured cloud backup reachable from the first exploitation server at 85.120.216[.]8.
- Key detection opportunities from the article: sqlservr.exe spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell is a high-fidelity signal for the xp_cmdshell chain. High-entropy DNS queries from database service identities indicate active tunneling. rclone or unauthorized cloud-sync binaries on servers warrant immediate investigation. OAuth device-code grants without corresponding enrollment events indicate T1598 phishing. Unauthorized reads of SAM, SYSTEM, SECURITY hives or ntds.dit by service accounts are critical alerts. For the fraud infrastructure specifically, URL parameters matching the schema ?ref=, venc=, v=, v0=, kwh= on lookalike utility domains are a structural indicator of the invoice fraud platform's output.
Full IOC table (IPs, domains, SHA-256 hashes for all beacon and agent variants, qTox IDs) and the complete MITRE ATT&CK mapping are in the SOCRadar report. Prioritize hunting for AdaptixC2 gopher agent artifacts (gopher_new.exe SHA-256 54caa256483876debd21c264bfc31bd96f925b2167f6d9358ab7ee0c87e6e37b, beacon.dll SHA-256 d566ccdd099b0decb7e7288c20097f34da2613e3ffe8c5acbc1a1d01b6fe217c) and block the four operation server IPs: 85.120.216[.]8, 91.92.241[.]187, 91.92.241[.]184, and 185.242.3[.]14.

item.title: A Closer Look at Malware From the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign, (Fri, Sep 25th)
item.description:
The Macfinger ClickFix campaign is delivering an unidentified macOS information stealer distinct from AMOS Stealer, actively targeting macOS 27.0 (Golden Gate) with a multi-stage shell script loader chain and websocket-based C2 exfiltration.
Key findings:
- The infection chain starts at the fake CAPTCHA domain hollow-badger-moasfraum[.]life, which clipboard-injects a Terminal command. That command pulls a shell script loader from hxxp[:]//45.131.215[.]56/8031e818c7a46?force=1, which then checks uname -m and fetches the architecture-appropriate Mach-O binary: arm64 from hxxp[:]//45.131.215[.]56/a7a11f95?force=1 or x86_64 from hxxp[:]//45.131.215[.]56/4e04813226b1b93?force=1. The C2 address is base64-encoded inside the loader script itself.
- Persistence is established via a LaunchAgent plist at /Users/[username]/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.softwareupdated.plist, executing a binary dropped at /Users/[username]/Library/Caches/com.apple.softwareupdate/SoftwareUpdate. The initial staging location is /Users/[username]/Library/Caches/com.apple.securityd/com.apple.periodic. Notably, three on-disk copies of the binary carry different SHA-256 hashes and slightly different file sizes despite appearing functionally identical, suggesting per-drop mutation.
- Post-infection C2 traffic hits hxxp[:]//95.163.153[.]80:8133 across three endpoints: /api/t for check-in and execution status (exec_start, exec_ok), /api/credentials for encrypted data exfiltration via HTTP POST, and /api/shell/agent. The User-Agent is Go-http-client/1.1. A protocol upgrade to websocket traffic is requested during the session, a behavior that separates this stealer from AMOS and is a strong network detection anchor.
- The malware solicits a broad permission sweep via macOS TCC prompts: Notes.app control via bash, Documents/Desktop/Downloads folder access via Terminal.app, Apple Music library, photo library, administrator password via a fake System Error dialog, and a separate macOS Keychain password prompt. Any of these TCC permission grants will appear in the TCC.db at /Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db and the user-level equivalent, making them forensic artifacts that survive binary removal.
- Five SHA-256 hashes are documented in the report: shell script loader (c6da028e0a8a25a35efa28ba508a556d1b53d1e61113c0aaebf31a49a5668912), x86_64 binary (457ed02b0a63ccf872e8459c91e2d1d6844a75414358849333f518cc538055b7), arm64 binary from the hosting URL (5a2242b862ef52fe7a08af596198412a7676c948bcd64a25ce5d2e6d4b35c6fb), first on-disk arm64 copy (3e26e006210ed398f98c090e9f1c982e76b3b73f1ce3e04ee1bf8d45c56e1a89), and the persistent binary (4a5952849232691849ed900609d7ff271ce296fe3cee4a81b58c28f2839fb5b6).
Hunt priority: check LaunchAgents for com.apple.softwareupdated.plist and the two Caches paths listed above, then pivot to TCC.db to confirm which permissions were granted. On the network side, alert on Go-http-client/1.1 User-Agent combined with websocket upgrade requests to port 8133. The full IOC list, a pcap of the infection traffic, and malware samples are available in the report.

item.title: How Cloudflare addressed a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability in Containers
item.description:
Cloudflare Containers had skip_block_zeroing enabled on dm-thin storage pools, letting a Workers Paid tenant recover up to 60 KiB of residual data per block from prior customers, including SQLite databases and directory structures.

Foreign actors breached a U.S. 🇺🇸 ICS integrator between March and April 2025, staging ~800 files across nine archives including customer SCADA configs and schematics. One integrator compromise can expose dozens of downstream utilities.

item.title: The Stealer Factory: Unpacking a Python-Based MaaS Infostealer Builder
item.description:
A Python-based MaaS infostealer builder lets low-skill operators compile customized credential stealers with XOR-obfuscated webhooks, dual persistence, and anti-VM evasion baked in at build time.
Key findings:
- The builder ships as a nested archive (my new program called 2.rar containing TokenGrabberBuilder.zip) with a GUI that auto-installs dependencies via pip at runtime, stores the operator's webhook URL in webhook.txt in the working directory, XOR-encodes it with key 0x5A then Base64-encodes it before injecting it into the payload, and offers three output modes: Nuitka (compiles to native machine code, defeats uncompyle6 and decompile3), PyInstaller (recoverable .pyc, unpackable with pyinstxtractor), or raw stealer.py for manual deployment. The interface explicitly labels Nuitka as "slower, stronger AV evasion," making the evasion intent explicit in the product itself.
- The payload's _debug_check() function runs four pre-execution environment checks: IsDebuggerPresent() via ctypes, process-name blacklisting for VirtualBox/Xen/QEMU/Parallels artifacts via psutil, a disk-size heuristic that exits if total capacity is under 50 GB, and a PID-derived variable sleep to outlast sandbox timeouts. All sensitive strings, including registry paths, SQL queries, and API endpoints, are stored as Base64-plus-XOR blobs decoded at runtime into the _E dictionary, and high-risk imports are loaded lazily through getter functions rather than at startup.
- Persistence uses two independent mechanisms: a Registry Run key written to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run under the deceptive name "WindowsUpdate," and an ONLOGON scheduled task created with creationflags=0x08000000 (CREATE_NO_WINDOW) with stdout and stderr redirected to DEVNULL. Both survive reboots independently, so removing one does not clean the infection.
- Data harvesting targets 17 Chromium-based browsers (Login Data, History, Web Data, Cookies via DPAPI and AES-256-GCM decryption), Firefox profiles (places.sqlite, cookies.sqlite in plaintext), Discord tokens via LevelDB scanning and regex with live validation against /api/v9/users/@me, Roblox .ROBLOSECURITY cookies validated before packaging, and Wi-Fi passwords via netsh wlan show profiles key=clear. All harvested material is assembled in memory as StolenData_USERNAME.zip using Python's BytesIO to avoid touching the filesystem, then POSTed to the XOR-decoded webhook URL.
- Three IOCs are listed in the report: MD5 hashes 610f0c65a3f8e88559f89ed90ea9ee5c and 429ed63ab3fbda8d22d0ac750ecfe8cc (Password-Stealer 006dba241) and 9ffe0e45c7a3f20e4481206c1c3b0854 (Trojan 006e632e1).
For response and hunting: query EDR and process logs for pip.exe spawned by non-development parent processes, creation of a Run key value named "WindowsUpdate" under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, and schtasks activity with ONLOGON triggers tied to Python interpreters. Recover webhook.txt from the working directory if the builder was run locally. For the payload, hunt for Python processes making outbound HTTP POST requests to webhook endpoints and accessing SQLite files under browser profile directories. Because the exfil ZIP is constructed entirely in memory, filesystem forensics will not catch it in transit. Focus on network telemetry, DNS, and proxy logs for POST traffic to Discord or unknown webhook infrastructure. Full IOC list is in the report.
#DFIR_Radar | View on X: https://x.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2103334559165083798
